claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 16 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 16 and in approved education
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first question in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first important question:

**How old is your child (or the youngest child if you have multiple children)?**

This will help determine which rules apply to your situation. Please let me know:
- The child's age, or
- Whether they are under 16, 16-19, or 20 or older

If you have multiple children of different ages, we can assess each one as we go through the questions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I'd like to check about my son Alex. He's 16, just turned 16 this year actually.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context! So Alex is 16 years old - that's helpful. Let me navigate to the next step.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age group, I need to check whether he's in full-time education or training, or if he qualifies under any extension criteria.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?**

For example:
- Is he in school, college, or university studying full-time?
- Is he on an apprenticeship or other training scheme?
- Or has he left education/training recently?

Please let me know his current situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in college doing his A-levels. He's in full-time education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in full-time education at college doing A-levels. Let me move to the next step to check the education level requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! A-levels are an approved qualification for Child Benefit purposes. This is great - Alex's education qualifies.

Now I need to check one more thing about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working full-time (i.e., working 24 hours or more per week)?**

This is an important check because if a 16-19 year old in education is also working full-time, they would no longer qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all. He's just focusing on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is not working, so that's perfectly fine. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is not working, he meets this requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

In other words, is he not claiming any of these benefits for himself?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits himself. He's just a student living at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is not receiving any of those benefits. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's doing A-levels at college, I expect the answer is no - but I need to confirm this to move forward.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not doing an apprenticeship. Just his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Now we need to check the claimant's residency requirements - that's about you as the person claiming Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. There are several possible paths that could make you eligible:

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

Or, if you don't normally live in the UK, do any of these apply to you:
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
- You have pre-settled status and are working/job-seeking/studying/have sufficient resources?
- You're a Crown servant living abroad?

Let me start with the main question: **Are you normally resident in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You're normally resident in the UK, which means you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. There are a few ways this can be satisfied:

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means one of the following:
- You live with him, OR
- You contribute to his upkeep (e.g., pay for his food, clothes, housing, pocket money), OR
- You're paying maintenance towards his care under a court order or agreement

Based on your earlier comment that Alex is "a student living at home," I assume you live with him - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim for him?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in any of these situations:**
- In hospital?
- In care (such as residential care)?
- Fostered with another family?
- Or is he living normally at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally at home with me. Nothing unusual about his living situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, the council is not providing support for where he lives or his upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything. I'm supporting him myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final check completed. Based on all the information you've provided, I can now confirm your eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me provide you with the final assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex

### Summary
You meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex. Here's why:

**About Alex:**
- He is 16 years old and in full-time approved education (A-levels at college)
- He is not working full-time
- He is not receiving any benefits in his own right
- He is living at home with you
- No one else is claiming for him

**About You:**
- You are normally resident in the UK (Manchester)
- You are responsible for Alex (he lives with you)
- You are the sole claimant
- The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps

To claim Child Benefit for Alex, you need to:

1. **Apply online** at [www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim) or **by post using form CH2**

2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex

3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate**

4. **Important note about income:** Be aware of the **High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may have to pay back some or all of the benefit through tax

5. **Payment frequency:** You'll receive payments every 4 weeks

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit, or do you have any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for?

reasonings: Alex is 16 years old and in full-time approved education (A-levels at college), which qualifies him as a dependent child. He is not working full-time (working less than 24 hours per week). He is not receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in his own right. He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. You are normally resident in the UK (Manchester), you are responsible for Alex (he lives with you at home), you are the only person claiming for him, he is living normally at home, and the local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are met.
